title: Torsion-free coherent modules on regular curves are locally free
statement: Let $X$ be an integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] scheme of topological dimension at most one and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Then $\mathcal F$ is torsion-free (its torsion subsheaf $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}$ of [lem-sc-torsion-subsheaf-quotient] is zero) if and only if it is finite locally free. The rank of this locally free module is constant and equals $\dim_{k(X)}\mathcal F_\eta$ at the generic point $\eta$, where $k(X)$ is the function field [def-sc-function-field].

source.place: Tag 0CC4 (divisors-lemma-torsion-free-over-regular-dim-1); constant rank on connected schemes is immediate from local constancy

proof.text: For every point $x\in X$, regularity makes $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ a regular Noetherian local domain. The topological dimension bound gives $\dim R\le1$. If $\dim R=0$, then the maximal ideal is zero and $R$ is a field. If $\dim R=1$, then $R$ is a discrete valuation ring by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. Coherence makes $\mathcal F_x$ a finitely generated $R$-module.

source.place: Tag 0CC4, proof: regular local rings on a scheme of dimension at most one are fields or discrete valuation rings

proof.text: Assume $\mathcal F$ is torsion-free. By [lem-sc-torsion-subsheaf-quotient] the stalk at $x$ of $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}$, which is zero, is the torsion submodule of $\mathcal F_x$ over the domain $R$, so each $\mathcal F_x$ is torsion-free over $R$. In the field case it is automatically finite free; in the DVR case [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] makes it finite free. Thus every stalk is finite free, and [lem-sc-coherent-free-stalks-locally-free] gives that $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free.

source.place: Tag 0CC4, proof: finitely generated torsion-free stalks over DVRs are free and a coherent sheaf with free stalks is locally free

proof.text: Conversely, if $\mathcal F$ is finite locally free, every stalk is a finite free module over the domain $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ (integrality gives the domain property), hence has no nonzero element killed by a nonzero scalar. So the torsion submodule of every stalk is zero, and by [lem-sc-torsion-subsheaf-quotient] every stalk of $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}$ is zero; a sheaf with zero stalks is zero, so $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}=0$ and $\mathcal F$ is torsion-free.

source.place: Tag 0CC4, converse: a locally free sheaf on an integral scheme is torsion-free

proof.text: The rank of a finite locally free sheaf is locally constant. Since an integral scheme is irreducible and therefore connected, this locally constant rank is constant. On the generic point, the stalk is a vector space over $k(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$, and its dimension is exactly that constant rank. Hence the rank equals $\dim_{k(X)}\mathcal F_\eta$.

lean.statement: theorem regular_curve_torsionfree_iff_finiteLocallyFree (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] (hregular : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.affineOpens, x ∈ U.1 ∧ IsRegularRing Γ(X, U)) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (F : X.Modules) (hcoherent : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F) : ((∀ (x : X) (s : F.presheaf.stalk x) (a : X.presheaf.stalk x), a ≠ 0 → a • s = 0 → s = 0) ↔ F.IsFiniteLocallyFree) ∧ (F.IsFiniteLocallyFree → F.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (Module.finrank X.functionField (F.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X))))
